summary: @servicetitan/startup-utils preinstall fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares `"preinstall": "node setup.mjs"`, which runs on `npm install`. setup.mjs is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style hex variable names such as `_0x488df8`/`_0x52943e` and rotated string-lookup objects hiding constants like `utf8`, `ldd`, `/etc/os-release`, `unzip`, `powershell`). At install time it downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, extracts and chmod+x's the binary, then invokes that Bun binary against a tarball-shipped `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB single-line file marked `// @bun @bun-cjs` so it will only execute under Bun, and its body is heavily obfuscated (string-array + rotation via a `WV8StW` shuffler over a ~1000-entry hex/string array, hex-mangled identifiers, and embedded `with` blocks that break strict-mode ES parsers and webcrack). The package's advertised purpose is a ~1.5KB semver-mismatch helper, which has no need for an alternate JavaScript runtime or a 727KB payload. Fetching a second language runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated sibling script under it is the alternate-runtime-dropper shape and lets the payload bypass Node-based static analysis. The scope `@servicetitan/*` is a corporate namespace whose legitimate maintainers do not ship obfuscated Bun-only payloads for a trivial helper, consistent with a compromised-publish supply-chain incident.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
